Wir bieten dir eine interessante, verantwortungsvolle und abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit bei einem modernen IT-Dienstleister mit attraktiven Anstellungsbedingungen, flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und vielseitigen Möglichkeiten zur Weiterentwicklung.
## Deine Aufgaben ##
#### Was dich erwartet ####
* Mitarbeit als Product Owner im Value Hub Claims mit Verantwortung für den Solution Stream Sumex
* Führen und Gestalten der dir zugewiesenen Produkte hinsichtlich Qualität und Weiterentwicklung
* Verantwortung für den Kundenkontakt und die Positionierung des Produkts am Markt im End-to-End-Prozess; Erkennen relevanter Kundenbedürfnisse und Marktentwicklungen sowie Bearbeiten von Eskalationen zum Produkt
* Vorbereitung, Verwaltung und Priorisierung des Produkt-Backlogs; Planung der Aktivitäten im Einklang mit dem mittel- und langfristigen Plan der Organisation sowie Abstimmung des Scopes mit den Kunden
* Definition und Überwachung von KPIs zur Bewertung des Produkterfolgs
* Sicherstellen von termingerechten und budgetkonformen Umsetzungen durch enge Abstimmung mit den Teams und kontinuierliches Monitoring im Rahmen des PI
## Deine Skills ##
#### Was du fachlich mitbringst ####
* Erfahrung als Product Owner, idealerweise mit praktischem Know-how im Arbeiten in einem SaFe-Scaled Agile Framework
* Vertieftes Versicherungswissen im Leistungsbereich, Kenntnisse der Branchensoftware Sumex sind von Vorteil
* Erfahrung in der Anforderungsdefinition und Zusammenarbeit mit Softwarelieferanten und Entwicklungsteams
* Aus- oder Weiterbildung in Betriebswirtschaft, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder Ähnliches
* Strukturierte und selbstständige Arbeitsweise und Motivation, mit agiler Arbeitsmethodik (Erfahrung/Zertifizierung SAFe wünschenswert) zu arbeiten und Veränderungen mitzugestalten
#### Was dich persönlich ausmacht ####
* Hohes Mass an Eigeninitiative, Bereitschaft zur Verantwortungsübernahme und Flexibilität
* Fähigkeit, mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern aus Business und IT zusammenzuarbeiten
* Analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten sowie eine hohe Organisationskompetenz
* Stufengerechte Kommunikation und Durchsetzungsstärke gegenüber Geschäftskunden, internen und externen IT-Spezialisten sowie Lieferanten

Die Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben sowie die Gesundheit unserer Mitarbeitenden sind uns wichtig. Fortschrittliche Arbeitsbedingungen und Benefits sind Teil unserer Wertschätzung für den Einsatz jedes Einzelnen. Dabei fördern wir flexible Arbeitsmodelle, eine moderne Infrastruktur und einen gesunden Ausgleich.

## Der Bewerbungsprozess ##
Der persönliche Kontakt, transparente Informationen sowie zeitnahe Rückmeldungen sind für uns das A und O im Bewerbungsprozess:
* Nach Eingang deiner Bewerbung, hörst du innert weniger Arbeitstage von uns
* In einem ersten Gespräch vor Ort oder remote tauschst du dich mit dem direkten Vorgesetzten zu Stellenprofil, Aufgaben und deinen Perspektiven aus.
* Stimmt es für dich und uns so weit, geht es einen Schritt weiter.
* Im Zweitgespräch bei uns in Solothurn lernst du Team, Vorgesetzte und HRM persönlich kennen und erhältst weitere Informationen zu Arbeitsplatz und Anstellungsbedingungen.
* Nach gegenseitig positivem Feedback unterbreiten wir dir ein Vertragsangebot.
* Bei Stellenantritt erwarten dich unser Welcome Day sowie ein koordiniertes Onboarding-Programm mit Teamkollegen, Fachexperten und Paten, welche dich in der ersten Zeit begleiten.

At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of Newsweek's Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces .
We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.
Ready to join us?

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Athlete Performance group. You’ll be responsible for a product suite that supports sports scientists and coaches in capturing and analysing athlete monitoring data—whether from wearables, optical tracking, or other data sources—to mitigate injury risk, optimise athletic performance, and track the physical development of athletes.

s.h: As a Senior Product Manager , you’ll
s.t:
Grow our human performance business . You’ll work with a cross-functional team to create a coherent product strategy and vision, connecting it to the wider company strategy and effectively delivering against it. You’ll “quarterback” a key investment, with the goal of building products that customers love and use daily.
Advocate for the product. You’ll develop a deep understanding of our customers and our business needs, building trusting relationships with customers and senior internal stakeholders. You’ll also help practitioners tell a fully contextualised story by combining athlete monitoring data with Hudl’s unique video and match analysis assets.
Motivate your squad . This is critical—you’ll determine what success looks like and work across multiple functions to turn your product vision to reality.
Foster collaboration. While balancing cost, timeline and customer benefit, you’ll also work with Marketing, Sales and Customer Support to develop go-to-market plans.
Time spent collaborating with your teammates in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We’re currently considering applicants within commuting distance of London. You’ll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.
Must-Haves
Experience . You’ve spent more than four years in product management roles within agile software development environments. You can work largely autonomously, and you have a proven track record of delivering valuable customer-facing software.
Dependable. You can be counted on to find the right information to make a decision, and you own them after they’re made.
Grit. You don’t let setbacks get you down—instead, you come through and deliver for customers.
A self-starter. You can balance your time between working with your squad, running discovery and defining strategy. You also know how to get the job done and can roll up your sleeves and get hands on when necessary.
AI-native. You leverage AI tools and workflows to accelerate discovery, sharpen decision-making, enhance communication, and increase delivery velocity. You know how to use AI to prototype ideas quickly, synthesize insights from data and customer feedback, and improve both product strategy and execution while maintaining strong judgment and ownership.
A communicator. You’re comfortable presenting, writing strategic documents, and sharing your product roadmap with stakeholders. You can decompose complex problems to bring senior leaders along, gain buy-in for your ideas, and motivate others toward a common goal.
Commercially-minded. You have good business sense and know how to balance user needs with business goals.
Naturally curious. You never stop learning—you’re eager for knowledge and new ideas because that improves the way you work. You love building prototypes, testing, learning and evolving.
Data-driven . You have a passion for using data and insights to drive high quality decision-making, but also know when to take calculated leaps of faith.
A proven people leader . You care deeply about your team and want to help them be successful.
Collaborative. You’re comfortable working with other teams, seek to understand the strengths of those around you, and have made each team you’ve worked on better. You relish tackling hard problems alongside your squad and building great relationships with teams.
Nice-to-Haves
Domain experience. If you’ve worked in the sports technology industry, or have experience in wearables, athlete tracking technologies, and the associated software, that’s a plus.
Sports science background. You have hands-on experience as a sports scientist and you bring deep industry context, along with a strong network of professional connections.
Innovation. You’ve successfully brought “0 to 1” product initiatives to life, turning concepts into real, impactful solutions.
Our Role
Champion work-life harmony . We’ll give you the flexibility you need in your work life (e.g., flexible vacation time, company-wide holidays and timeout (meeting-free) days, remote work options and more) so you can enjoy your personal life too.
Guarantee autonomy . We have an open, honest culture and we trust our people from day one. Your team will support you, but you’ll own your work and have the agency to try new ideas.
Encourage career growth . We’re lifelong learners who encourage professional development. We’ll give you tons of resources and opportunities to keep growing.
Provide an environment to help you succeed . We've invested in our offices, designing incredible spaces with our employees in mind. But whether you’re at the office or working remotely, we’ll provide you the tech stack and hardware to do your best work.
Support your wellbeing. Depending on location, we offer medical and retirement benefits for employees—but no matter where you’re located, we have resources like our Employee Assistance Program and employee resource groups to support your mental health.

Senior Product Manager
You will play a pivotal marketing role at Diagnostic X-Ray (DXR) and drive creation of solutions (integrated combination of products and services) from idea to market. You will be accountable for defining, launching and building profitable product solutions that transform healthcare.

You will work directly with the different functions within the organization and maintains a balanced development scope. This will not only ensure the products/solutions are developed to the feature and price specifications that each target market segment demands but also will deliver a profitable and performing product in all its aspects.
The Product Manager owns the product lifecycle from concept phase through development and launch and eventually, end of life. You are required to have expertise in market segmentation, product strategy, competitive strategy, and product development.

Join corporate core teams to drive implementation (plan, execute, track, and communicate) of strategic marketing initiatives at DXR.
Own your product and its performance during its complete lifecycle from concept phase throughout development and launch, till end of life.
Support and drive upstream marketing activities for the solution, including definition of the strategy and its enablers as well as its alignment with key markets globally.
Translate in-depth customer and market insights to support the product strategy: analyze the customers, markets, the competition, and the trends to create winning concepts, value propositions and clear product specifications to ensure delivering according to the customer’s needs and expectations.
Drive the development of business cases to prioritize investments
Interact with various disciplines including Research, R&D departments, internal and external design agencies, suppliers, industrialization, marketing management, marketing communication and international sales organizations.
Be a key core team member in product development and lifecycle management teams.
Drive the market readiness as part of PDLM. Ensure completion of appropriate deliverables (feature descriptions, value propositions, costing/pricing/quoting materials, etc.)
Follow a lean way of working and a continuous improvement mindset within the product management team.
You are a part of The Diagnostic X-ray product management team of Philips Healthcare and become part of the global marketing department. You will be based in Pune and report into the Head of Product Management and be working in an international network of various stakeholders based across the globe. The team operates in an open, ‘can-do’ atmosphere. The team is characterized by a “self-starting” mentality.
In the team we focus on translating the customer voice in medical products, solutions and services. We manage a wide Radiography and Fluoroscopy portfolio targeting the global health market contributing directly to the growth of the business.

Bachelor or master’s degree in marketing, business administration, medical engineering or similar
5 to 10 years related experience in product management and marketing in the medical device industry
Ability to relate and communicate with different levels and functions in the organization to drive the development of market leading solutions.
Ability to take ownership, identify, and remove roadblocks regardless of direct responsibilities
Expertise delivering complex projects to meet demanding cost, quality and introduction date targets
Ability to motivate, guide and drive project teams working on complex projects to successful outcomes
Highly entrepreneurial; both analytical and hands-on to driving business growth (result oriented)
Ability to assess and synthesize customer needs and feedback, translate those into a winning value proposition and actionable solution specifications; comfortable with making tradeoffs, decisively
Ability to excite sales teams and customers with ideas about new products (and transfer those ideas to Best in Class Marcom and Training materials)
Ability to work well under pressure and deliver to deadlines
Excellent communication skills (sending and receiving)
Strong in English language

Define, communicate, and maintain product goals, and priorities.
Manage the complete software product lifecycle, including ideation, requirements definition, development, release, adoption, optimization, and end\-of\-life planning.

Lead product planning and prioritization across large, highly interconnected projects and product platforms, ensuring alignment of dependencies, risks, and business outcomes.

Stakeholder Engagement \& Product Performance

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Data Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Additional education or training in Product Management, Agile methodologies, or Business Administration is advantageous.
Certification such as Professional Scrum Product Owner (PSPO), Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), or equivalent is a benefit.

5\+ years of experience in software product management, product ownership, or similar roles, including experience as a Senior Product Owner.
Proven success delivering complex enterprise software products in agile development environments.

About MoonPay
MoonPay is for builders with something to prove.
This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia.
AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.
You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.
The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents.

The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running

About the Opportunity
In this role, you will join MoonPay’s Crypto Asset Management team as a Product Manager, helping us build and scale the liquidity and asset infrastructure that supports products across MoonPay.
The team is responsible for how liquidity is sourced and distributed across our platform, supporting high-value crypto transaction volumes across multiple assets, venues, and blockchains. As our remit expands across products including Ramps, Swaps, and Enterprise, the volume and complexity of product work is growing with it.
You will take ownership of day-to-day product execution across our on-chain and off-chain workstreams, helping turn business and technical requirements into clearly defined, prioritised, and executable work.
Working closely with the Principal Product Manager, Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, and commercial teams, you will support initiatives including liquidity-provider integrations, asset availability, routing and best-execution capabilities, custody and wallet infrastructure, and the broader on-chain services required to operate reliably at scale.
Your work will help the team move faster, improve the efficiency and resilience of our liquidity infrastructure, and enable MoonPay to support significantly more products and transaction volume as the business grows.
This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, wants to deepen their understanding of crypto and financial infrastructure, and is excited to develop their product craft in a fast-moving, high-impact environment.

Own day-to-day product execution across Crypto Asset Management initiatives, translating business, technical, operational, and compliance requirements into clear product requirements, user stories, project plans, and delivery milestones.
Support integrations with new liquidity sources , including centralised exchanges, OTC trading desks, and decentralised services, helping expand MoonPay’s liquidity network and improve sourcing efficiency, reliability, and execution.
Coordinate asset availability and infrastructure initiatives across Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, Commercial, and other Product teams, ensuring dependencies, decisions, risks, and requirements are understood and tracked through delivery.
Support the setup and evolution of technical infrastructure across areas such as wallets, gas sponsorship, transaction broadcasting, and other on-chain infrastructure services, working closely with engineering and operational teams to translate requirements into scalable product solutions.
Support roadmap development and prioritisation , using data, commercial value, operational requirements, customer impact, risk, and engineering constraints to help determine which initiatives should be addressed first.
Contribute to the evolution of our liquidity and asset-management infrastructure , including custody and wallet capabilities, liquidity routing, best execution, settlement efficiency, monitoring, and risk-management tooling.
Use data to evaluate product performance and opportunities , identifying friction, operational inefficiencies, or areas where product and infrastructure improvements can create measurable value for MoonPay and its customers.

Must-have experience and skills
You have experience working in product management, product operations, treasury, finance, business analysis, technical programme delivery, or a similar role , and can take a problem from initial requirements through to structured execution.
You are comfortable working across cross-functional teams , particularly with Engineering, Operations, Compliance, Finance, Treasury, or Commercial stakeholders, and can turn complex or ambiguous requirements into clear actions and priorities.
You have strong product thinking and analytical skills , with the ability to understand trade-offs, use data to support decisions, and prioritise work based on business and customer impact.
You have a genuine interest in crypto, fintech, or financial infrastructure and are motivated to build a deeper understanding of areas such as blockchain networks, liquidity, exchanges, custody, wallets, and digital-asset infrastructure.
Nice-to-have experience
Previous exposure to crypto or fintech infrastructure , particularly liquidity management, exchange or OTC integrations, stablecoins, custody, wallets, or DeFi protocols.
Familiarity with regulated financial products, crypto compliance requirements, blockchain infrastructure, or products handling high-value financial transactions.

Our Trust & Safety, Integrity and Fraud Product team is dedicated to ensuring a safe and trusted experience for all customers across our platform, including Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers.

We tackle complex challenges, from preventing fraud, abuse and Account Takeover to ensuring authenticity, to building regulatory compliance capabilities, all while balancing risk mitigation and providing a seamless user experience.

Our team partners closely with cross-functional groups, including Engineering, Data Science, Compliance, and Risk Operations, to drive strategic initiatives that protect our business while fostering growth.

Trust is foundational to an on-demand marketplace. Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt are converging European capabilities into one platform and one global product capability to prevent fraud and abuse.

The marketplace is expanding rapidly beyond just restaurants as we become “your door to more." As we add new products, geographies, ways for Consumers, Merchants and Couriers to engage, we’re expanding and enhancing our fraud capabilities to be best in the industry at keeping our platform safe and trustworthy.

We strongly believe that trust is the most important attribute of an online marketplace, and the team ensures that we maintain this trust.
We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager that will lead dedicated cross-functional teams to solve complex challenges that impact Consumers, Couriers and Merchants and touch every corner of our business - from new user onboarding, to the in-app delivery experience, to the products and services being created that our users can’t find anywhere else.

We are looking to hire for a few roles, so you’ll either lead a vertical fraud team protecting Consumers, Couriers or Merchants, or lead a horizontal fraud platform team focused on building our Risk Engine, Data Signals Intelligence and Automation / Anomaly Detection capabilities or leading compliance and authenticity efforts involving Identity Verification and Right to Work.

The Fraud team is in hyper growth in terms of its size and impact and offers a unique opportunity to set and execute on a vision that will shape the future of Deliveroo, DoorDash and Wolt globally.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Set the vision and long-term product strategy for one of our vertical fraud teams or our horizontal platform fraud team.
Prevent, detect and mitigate fraud and abuse, building and leveraging AI systems to address risk in real time.
Build an AI-led fraud operations platform that turns complex marketplace signals into automated decisions, prioritised investigations, and actionable case workflows, stopping fraud, abuse and manipulation before incidents occur.
Develop and execute a customer-focused product roadmap through close collaboration with senior leadership, Operations, Data Science, Analytics, Design, and Engineering all while balancing business needs.
Translate customer and internal-user needs into clear, well-defined functional and technical requirements backed by data analysis and deep understanding of our users
Guide and interface closely with data analysis and engineering teams to define scope, review and refine technical capabilities, prioritize projects for release, and define new opportunities.
Build long-term instrumentation, monitoring, and evaluation capabilities for product performance, tracking, and to create product insights.
Establish business cases and projected return on investment to identify and prioritize opportunities
Partner with Finance and Business Leaders to manage the impact on the profitability of the overall business.
Establish success metrics and executive reviews covering fraud trends and P&L impact.

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. Now we need a PM who wants to take that further, in a market being rewritten in real time.
Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. Nobody has really figured out what reliability means for this kind of software yet. That's the problem you'd own.
As a Product Manager, you will be responsible for empowering developers and designers to solve customer problems. You will work directly with our SVP Product Engineering Daniel .

Shape company and product strategy alongside our SVP of Product Engineering. It's a genuine partnership: you'll develop the vision for where Checkly goes next, decide where we play in the AI testing, monitoring, and observability landscape and where we don't, and turn that into a direction. You build the strategy with us, not execute someone else's.
Shape Checkly's point of view on reliability in an AI-native world: how teams monitor AI-generated code, agent-driven workflows, and LLM-backed features
Lead initiatives across Product Engineering, Sales and Marketing, and represent Checkly directly to customers and in developer communities.
Live in the product and the problem. Empathy for DevOps, SRE and Platform Engineering isn't a line item. It's the job.
You ship with AI where it helps and know when not to. You don't just talk about it.
What you should have
You've built software before this. You're an ex-engineer, ex-founder, or ex-solutions engineer who has written real code and shipped real things, and now you want to own the product. This one's non-negotiable: you should be able to reason about APIs, MCPs, CLIs, and how systems fit together without a translator.
You've worked in a startup, not just a big company. You're comfortable with ambiguity, small teams, and owning outcomes end to end. You don't need a big-company machine around you to be effective.
You've built technical products, ideally developer tools. Adjacent technical products count. Experience in monitoring or observability is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
New to the PM title? That's fine. If you're coming from a founding or solutions-engineering seat and want to go all-in on product, we want to hear from you.
You're technical enough to be dangerous with AI tooling. You can prototype in code, throw together a mock, or pressure-test technical viability yourself when it moves things forward.
FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. Need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment.

s.h: What you will hate about us
s.t:
We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.
We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.
We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.
We are lean, so you own the boring parts too. There is no PM ops layer to delegate the unglamorous work to. You will do strategy one hour and clean up a messy spec the next.
We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.
Customer signals come first, and most of the time they beat your gut. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up. Earn it by making customers happy, and then there is room for the moonshots. If you want to lead with your own bold bets, you will find this frustrating.

As our Global Product Manager for Sustaining Hardware within Philips Ambulatory & Monitoring Diagnostics (AM&D), you will be accountable for the ongoing lifecycle management of the MCT and Holter devices.

About Teramind
Teramind is a global leader in workforce intelligence, insider risk management, and data loss prevention. Used by thousands of companies across 60+ countries, our platform gives organizations the visibility to protect their people, their data, and their operations. We sit at the intersection of three converging markets - Insider Risk, DLP, and Workforce Analytics - and we are one of the few players that spans all three on a unified behavioral data layer.
The Teramind Endpoint Agent is one of the key differentiators of our platform. It runs on hundreds of thousands of endpoints across Windows, macOS, and Linux, capturing the behavioral signal that powers our detection, DLP enforcement, analytics, and AI. The depth and quality of what the Agent sees is a primary reason customers choose Teramind over the alternatives - and the product leader who owns it plays a pivotal role in the company's success.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the Teramind Endpoint Agent, and the AI Usage Control capabilities built on top of it, end to end.

You will be the single accountable product leader for the roadmap, priorities, and outcomes of the Agent organization - approximately half of Teramind engineering, working across operating systems, low-level platform components, and the server-side telemetry pipeline. This is a pivotal role.

The Agent is one of the strongest competitive moats Teramind has, and the next chapter of the product strategy depends on what we build into it. You are coming in to bring product rigor, customer insight, prioritization discipline, and technical judgment to a team that is capable of shipping world-class endpoint technology.

AI Usage Control is one of the most important things you will build here. Companies have spent twenty years governing what employees do with sensitive data, and they now have a second workforce: AI agents reading files, calling tools, and executing commands on the same machines, with none of the accountability.

Nobody has worked out what supervising them looks like, and much of it never touches the network, so the endpoint is the only place you can see it. You will own that end to end. You will sit alongside other product managers, reporting to the VP of Product. Together, you own Teramind's product surface area.
What You Will Own
The Agent roadmap across all platforms. Windows, macOS, Linux, and the platforms after them. You decide what ships, in what order, and why, balancing customer demand, platform modernization, performance, and security hardening on one prioritized backlog.
The endpoint layer of AI Usage Control . Detecting AI that never touches the network - native desktop clients, IDE-embedded assistants, terminal-based coding agents, AI-native Teramind | Senior Product Manager, AI and Endpoint browsers, and local models running offline - and capturing the prompts, pastes, uploads, and agent-executed commands that browser and network DLP cannot see.
Translating business vision into engineering reality . You turn signals from executives, sales, customers, competitors and the engineering org into a coherent technical roadmap. You are the interpreter between “we need to detect AI exfiltration” and “here is how we instrument the endpoint to see it.”
Building for the enterprise: bulletproof and undetectable . Enterprise customers expect the Agent to be invisible to end users, resilient against tampering, and reliable in conditions that break weaker products. You own the roadmap that keeps it that way.
Performance, footprint, and reliability. Every CPU cycle, megabyte and battery percent we consume is felt by the end user and argued about by the customer's IT team. You set and defend the performance bar.
Define, measure, and meet product KPIs. Adoption, rollout velocity, deployment success rate, crash rates, detection coverage, time-to-patch on OS changes. You set the numbers and hold the team and the company to them.
Industry and ecosystem relationships. Microsoft, Apple, the Linux ecosystem, MDM vendors, and the major AV and EDR vendors. You represent Teramind in technical conversations where the agent's architecture is the subject.

5+ years of product management experience , with at least 3 owning a technical platform, SDK, agent, or systems-level product. This is a senior IC seat: influence without headcount.
Technical depth is non-negotiable . You do not need to write C++, but you should reason about Windows architecture, macOS system extensions, and the trade-offs between Endpoint Security and Network Extension frameworks. You can push back credibly in a design review.
You understand how AI actually runs on a computer . A hosted model in a browser tab, a native desktop client, an IDE-embedded assistant, a CLI coding agent, and a local model under Ollama are five different detection problems, and several are invisible to anything watching the network. You know why, and you know what an audit trail for an autonomous agent has to capture.
Endpoint or systems background. You have shipped endpoint security (EDR, EPP, XDR), monitoring or management agents, OS-level tools, or systems software. CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Defender, Tanium and similar are directly relevant. Pure SaaS and application PMs without systems exposure will struggle here.
You think in outcomes, not features. Success is “95% of customers roll out a new agent version within 30 days,” not “shipped version 27.0.”
You are comfortable with security trade-offs. Visibility versus privacy, tamper protection versus usability, cloud processing versus on-device intelligence. You can hold the attacker's perspective and the IT buyer's perspective in the same conversation.
You work with AI, not just about it. You use AI in your own practice, prototyping to pressure-test concepts before spending engineering cycles, and evaluating model behavior rather than trusting vendor claims.
You bring rigor, and you write. PRDs, decision memos, prioritization frameworks, release cadence, credible engineering-facing specs. In a distributed team, writing is how product management scales.

Engineering background earlier in your career: systems, kernel, driver, or low-level platform work
Windows Filter Drivers, Minifilters or WFP; macOS Endpoint Security or Network Extensions; Linux eBPF, kernel modules or userspace agents
MDM ecosystems (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, Kandji)
Insider risk, DLP, or behavioral analytics
Local model runtimes and on-device inference (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp)
Agentic AI: tool calling, MCP, and autonomous coding or workflow agents
AI governance, AI security, or shadow AI discovery products
EDR and AV co-existence and exclusion lists at scale
Why This Role
Endpoint agents are having a moment. The convergence of insider risk, DLP, AI, and hybrid work is making the endpoint the most strategically important surface in enterprise security and workforce intelligence. Teramind's Agent is one of the deepest data-collection engines in the market - we see things the rest of the category does not - and it is one of the strongest competitive moats we have.

Our customers can start a pentest in as little as 24 hours and integrate with advanced development cycles thanks to the powerful combination of our SaaS platform coupled with an exclusive community of testers known as the Cobalt Core.

Description
All organizations need security testing for their software and we are building the world’s largest and smartest pentest management platform to help solve this challenge at scale.
As a Contract Senior Staff Product Manager , you will drive the definition, delivery, and adoption of new product features and ecosystem integrations. You will be responsible for taking the lead of our next gen deliverables, from user discovery and roadmap prioritization to go-to-market execution - ensuring that our platform evolves to solve the most pressing challenges in the security workflow.
This is a full-time contractor position providing hourly coverage from October through the end of February . In this role, you will merge attention to detail with the ability to understand and align business objectives, while working collaboratively with cross-functional teams to drive customer insights and inputs directly into the development process. You will work closely with our other Customer Experience and Pentester Experience teams.
What You Would Do
As a member of a growing team of product managers your responsibilities include:
Rapidly acquire new technical knowledge while maintaining meticulous attention to detail. Champion the strategic product direction across the organization, ensuring internal and external synchronization while serving as a subject matter expert on industry developments and defensive security operations.
Represent our customers. Work with Product Design, Product Marketing, Sales and Customer Success teams to bring the customer’s voice into the development process.
Manage the platform next-gent feature deliverables . Make tough tactical prioritization decisions while enabling the company to think long-term.
Collaborate across teams. We win or lose as a team. Product managers are a critical role in creating alignment between engineering teams and stakeholders.
Have familiarity with information security, security operations, vulnerability disclosure, vulnerability management and other security domain areas.
Become an expert in pentesting best practices. You are ready to discuss and demonstrate product details with developers, product designers, security operations, pentesters, customers and sales prospects.
Measure success. Own the measures used to define success for your product. Success measures must be defined at the inception of a product and tracked throughout its lifecycle. Make measures visible to all stakeholders and interpret them into actionable conclusions and new hypotheses.
Lead Go-to-Market (GTM) Readiness: Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to orchestrate successful feature launches. Develop launch strategies, create internal training materials, and support the creation of customer-facing collateral to ensure seamless adoption.
Maintain technical fluency in the operational workflows of modern cybersecurity tools, including vulnerability management or offensive security platforms. Evaluate how these tools function within a customer’s security environment to inform product development.

8+ years experience in Product Management and 3+ years experience in cybersecurity tools (vulnerability management or offensive security platforms), with a demonstrated ability to discover new opportunities and then define and deliver products. Experience in fast-growing software companies is a plus.
Strong technical skills - you can work alongside customers to help debug and improve our integration offerings.
Strong customer and stakeholder empathy. You must not only be the voice of the customer but at various times the voice of marketing, finance, engineering, sales and customer success. You must be able to channel many points of view.
Strong written and verbal communication skills. You’re great at explaining highly technical topics to technical and non-technical audiences, with a talent for building empathy for user problems.
Strong analytical capabilities is a plus.
Strong bias for action, creative thinking, innovation and data-driven product decision-making.
A can-do attitude and ability to juggle multiple priorities simultaneously.
Experience with agile software development.
Experience working with global team members (This team is a global team).
Hands-on experience with core cybersecurity tooling (e.g., DAST/SAST scanners, vulnerability management systems, or pentest workflow platforms). Articulate how security teams utilize these tools to identify, prioritize, and remediate risk, understanding the "why" behind the tooling workflow beyond simple API integrations.
Strong technical and product communication skills: Ability to translate complex security concepts into clear documentation, user guides, and release notes tailored to both technical developers and business stakeholders.
Full-time availability for the duration of the contract. You must be able to commit to full-time hourly coverage from October through the end of February, with no planned extended absences or vacations during the contract period (excluding recognized company holiday’s).

Data-Driven Optimisation – Analyse product usage and performance metrics to optimise payment features and uncover new market opportunities.
Process Evangelism & Mentorship – Advocate for thorough documentation and efficient workflows to help the team anticipate obstacles and ensure smooth product delivery.

This role needs someone who can hold both sides of payments: the consumer experience and the rails underneath it.
Product Experience – 3+ years as a Product Manager in payments, banking or fintech.
Launch & Scale Track Record – Proven experience shipping products from scratch and growing live products through their scaling phase.
Payments Fluency – Deep experience with at least one payment rail — card issuing, SEPA transfers or account-to-account — and enough familiarity with the mechanics behind them (authorisation and settlement, scheme flows, chargebacks and disputes) to hold a conversation with Engineering and providers alike.
Financial & Analytical Skills – Strong grasp of payment economics — interchange and scheme fees, provider costs, fraud losses — and the ability to build a business case and read performance data without waiting for BI.
Regulated-Environment Comfort – Ability to design great experiences within regulatory constraints (PSD2, SCA, AML) and to treat Compliance, Legal and Fraud as partners rather than gatekeepers.
Stakeholder Management – Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams (Engineering, UX, BI, Finance, Compliance).
Language Skills – Professional fluency in English. Italian isn't required — we work in English .
Don't worry if you don't tick every box. We believe in the power of different viewpoints and strengths. Your unique perspective is important as we build something special: if you're passionate and can make a difference, we truly encourage you to apply.

HelloFresh serves millions of customers weekly across 18 business units and 8 brands worldwide. At the heart of our product is a belief that every customer deserves a menu that feels like it was made for them, the right meals, at the right time, for the right person. We call it the Sous Chef vision.
As Senior PM II on the Personalization Experience team , you own what makes that vision real and felt . You're not building the ranking algorithm, you're building the experiences that make customers trust it, the data collection that makes it smart, and the moments where someone thinks: this app actually knows me .
This is a high-autonomy role at the intersection of consumer UX, engineering, and ML systems. The problems are genuinely hard, the scale is real, and the decisions are yours to make.

Food Profile Quality & Signal Collection: The food profile is the raw material that powers everything downstream. Your job is to move customers from "fields filled in" to truly Personalization-Ready: high-signal, validated, actionable. You'll own and iterate on the collection experiences that give our models the data they need to perform.
The "Sous Chef" Feel & Transparency: You build the moments where personalization becomes tangible, the places where we tell customers why certain meals were chosen for them. This isn't just UX work, it's trust infrastructure for the entire personalization stack.
Cross-Org Data Supplier : You're the clean, reliable interface between raw signal and downstream experience, owning the explanation payloads and API contracts that make it all work at scale. You operate across organizational boundaries and align on shared metrics without needing to own the surfaces.
AI-Native Discovery You use GenAI tools actively to compress discovery-to-decision cycles, synthesizing global customer signals, stress-testing hypotheses, and arriving at decision-ready specs faster than traditional PM workflows allow. You don't treat AI as a novelty; it's a genuine speed and quality multiplier in your daily practice.
Long-Horizon Strategy You manage your domain with real autonomy. You run a flywheel: better profile data → better models → more visible personalization → more signal back to personalization. You own the strategy and sequencing, not just the backlog, thinking 12–18 months out and making the calls that shape the direction of the team.

Deep personalization or data-collection PM experience. 5+ years of PM experience, with meaningful time on user-facing personalization or data collection products, ideally where the UX is the data pipeline, and where you've shipped for both end customers and downstream data consumers.
Strong product taste and customer-facing craft. You have a genuine feel for what makes a consumer experience compelling, trustworthy, and sticky, not just functional. You've built products at scale where millions of people interact with what you ship, and you hold a high bar for the details: the copy, the interaction pattern, the moment of delight. You know the difference between a feature that works and one that earns trust.
Data-native. You query your own data (SQL/Python), define your own input/output KPIs, and hold your own in deep-dive technical discussions without needing a data analyst to translate.
Cross-org credibility. You've shipped products across organizational boundaries, aligning on shared metrics, maintaining clean contracts with engineering partners, and navigating competing priorities without direct authority.
Experimentation with healthy skepticism. You design experiments to validate hypotheses and know how to interpret results without over-indexing on noise. You've made hard calls to kill features based on data.
Exceptional communicator. You can make a complex algorithmic concept legible to a non-technical VP and you can write a spec that engineers can actually ship from.
The AI edge. You've already incorporated AI-assisted workflows into your daily practice to increase speed, depth of insight, and output quality.

Solace cuts through the red tape of healthcare by pairing patients with expert advocates and giving them the tools to make better decisions—and get better outcomes.

Solace isn't a place to coast. We're here to redefine healthcare—and that demands urgency, precision, and heart. As a Technical Product Manager at Solace, you’ll take ownership of building and optimizing the systems that power our user experience and internal operations. You’ll operate at the intersection of data, product, and operations—diving deep into the funnel, asking hard questions, and translating complexity into clarity.
You’ll work cross-functionally with engineering, growth, care teams, and leadership to define, build, and launch features that drive measurable results. This is an ideal role for someone who loves building clean systems, thrives on details, and has the ambition to do their best work in a fast-moving startup environment.
You understand that even in a "move fast and break things" culture, there are certain things that cannot break—and you take pride in your power of observation and instinct for quality to ensure they don’t. This role reports to our Chief Product Officer.
This is a remote role, with relocation support available for candidates interested in relocating to the Redwood City/San Francisco area. Relocation is not required.

Own and manage technical product initiatives from ideation through execution, ensuring each project drives meaningful business outcomes.
Analyze data, validate hypotheses, understand user behavior, and define success metrics using tools such as SQL and dashboards.
Develop a deep understanding of Solace’s user funnel and internal systems, and identify opportunities for optimization and automation.
Translate complex operational and data requirements into clear product specs and technical requirements for engineering.
Prioritize ruthlessly and align stakeholders across engineering, operations, and growth to ship features quickly and effectively.
Monitor the performance of released features and iterate based on data and user feedback.
Maintain clear documentation and communication across teams to ensure alignment and accountability.

We are looking for a Product Manager to help shape the direction and continued evolution of TwinStream ’s products.
You will bring together customer needs, business opportunities, technical insight and delivery experience to create a clear, coherent product direction. Working across engineering, architecture, delivery, platform, service and commercial teams, you will ensure that product decisions deliver meaningful outcomes while strengthening the long-term value, usability and sustainability of our products.
This is not simply a backlog-management role. You will be responsible for understanding the problems that matter, defining the outcomes we need to achieve and helping teams make informed decisions about where to invest.
You will champion reusable, configurable product capabilities over unnecessary customer-specific solutions and help make our products progressively easier to understand, adopt, deploy, operate, support and extend.

Own and communicate a clear product vision, strategy and roadmap.
Translate customer, user, commercial and technical insight into prioritised product outcomes.
Define clear product principles and guardrails to support consistent decision-making.
Maintain awareness of relevant market, technology and competitor developments.
Identify opportunities to strengthen and differentiate TwinStream ’s product proposition.

Develop a strong understanding of our customers, users, prospects & operational environments.
Work with customers and internal stakeholders to understand underlying problems rather than accepting proposed solutions at face value.
Identify recurring customer needs that could become reusable core product capability.
Support commercial & business-development activity with clear product positioning and roadmap context.
Maintain USP in Cross Domain space.
Maintain SWOT analysis of the product.

Maintain an outcome-focused roadmap that provides clarity without constraining delivery teams.
Ensure the roadmap balances customer commitments, future opportunities, security, product evergreening, technical debt, operational efficiency and risk mitigation against market disruption.
Prioritise investment based on customer value, strategic alignment, commercial opportunity, risk and delivery effort.
Make transparent trade-offs between customer-specific delivery, core product investment, platform improvement and component evolution.
Ensure priorities, dependencies, assumptions and decisions are visible and understood.
Review roadmap progress regularly and adapt it as evidence, risks and priorities change.

Work closely with Product Oversight, delivery and engineering teams to provide clarity on the problem, intended outcome and product context.
With the Product Oversight team, help delivery teams determine whether requirements should become core product capability, configurable variation or customer-specific delivery.
Support shaping of initiatives, epics and features without prescribing detailed technical solutions.
Provide timely product decisions and remove ambiguity that could delay delivery.
Encourage experimentation, iterative delivery and early validation.
Ensure completed capabilities achieve the intended customer and product outcomes.

Protect the overall integrity and coherence of the product across components, customers and implementations.
Reduce duplication and fragmentation by promoting common patterns, reusable capabilities and standard approaches.
Ensure product decisions consider security, maintainability, usability, supportability, observability and operational cost.
Champion automation, self-service and repeatable deployment and configuration patterns.
Make product maintenance, lifecycle management and technical sustainability visible within prioritisation decisions.
Identify repeated delivery or operational pain points and ensure they are considered for simplification, standardisation or Productisation.

Build trusted relationships across customers, engineering, architecture, delivery, platform engineering, service management and business development.
Communicate product direction, priorities and decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Facilitate constructive discussions where customer demand, delivery constraints and strategic priorities compete.
Provide leadership with clear visibility of product progress, risks, opportunities and decisions.
Create alignment without relying on hierarchy or excessive governance.
You will be comfortable working in a technically complex environment and able to move between strategic thinking and practical delivery.

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions.
The team’s execution has been exceptional and we are scaling at a remarkable pace. Our early team brings experience from J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, PayPal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium and others, and we are backed by Accel, Lightspeed, NFX and other top-tier investors.

We are looking for a Product Operations for Latin America to own how new currencies and corridors actually get to market across the region. Every currency we launch unlocks new corridors for our institutional clients and drives trading volume and revenue directly.

Your mandate is to make that expansion happen on the ground: sourcing and onboarding liquidity providers, standing up settlement rails with banking partners, clearing jurisdiction-specific regulatory requirements, and holding every launch to the reliability bar our clients expect.
You will run the regional launch pipeline with real independence. You will own pricing inputs, sequencing and the go-live decision. You report to the Product Leader of Global Payments & Currencies, who sets strategic prioritisation for which currencies matter most based on payout corridor relevance. You own the how and the when.
If you have shipped cross-border payment products, worked with banking or card network infrastructure, or built API-driven financial products across jurisdictions, this role will feel familiar. The difference is that you will be doing it at the frontier of stablecoin-settled FX infrastructure, where the rails are new and the playbook is yours to write.

Own corridor launch, end to end. You own every currency in your regional pipeline from Alpha through General Availability. You track liquidity partner onboarding, settlement rail readiness, regulatory clearance, operational setup and pricing. You run readiness reviews, maintain the launch checklist, and make the go/no-go call.
Operationalise our licences. Holding a licence and being able to use it are two different things. You work with Product Management, Legal and Regulatory, Compliance, Finance and Engineering to turn each licence, registration and partner permission into permitted product scope, documented operating procedures and live client flows.

You keep what we are authorised to do and what we actually run in market in step, and you make sure new capability reaches clients as soon as the licence allows rather than months later.
Work directly with LPs and banking partners. You are the product voice in liquidity provider onboarding and banking partner discussions. You understand what it takes to stand up a new currency pair technically, what banking partners need in order to enable settlement, and how to translate partner constraints into product decisions.
Navigate multi-market regulatory complexity. Every currency carries jurisdiction-specific requirements. You work with Legal and Regulatory to establish what is needed, translate it into product and engineering decisions, and ensure no currency launches without clearance.
Prioritise engineering effort. You work with engineers to deliver against the roadmap. You write specs, set sprint priorities, and partner with your EM so capacity lands on the highest-impact currencies.
Drive post-launch adoption. A currency is not done at launch. You track whether clients are actually trading new corridors, partner with GTM to drive activation, find the friction, and feed what you learn back into prioritisation.
Build the regional launch playbook. You turn each launch into a repeatable, documented process covering every dependency, gate criterion and handoff, so the tenth currency is faster than the first.

Must-haves
8+ years in product management, product operations or programme management. You have owned a complex, multi-dependency delivery process in a B2B or infrastructure product.
Cross-border payments or financial infrastructure context. You have worked on payments, FX, card networks or digital asset products.
Multi-market experience. You have shipped products across multiple countries or regulatory jurisdictions.
Comfort operating between product, legal and compliance. You can read a regulatory requirement, work out what it means for a product flow, and drive it to a decision without waiting to be told.
Operational rigour. You maintain systems that track complex, multi-dependency work. You build the checklist, follow up on the open item, and catch the gap before it becomes a blocker.
Based in Brazil, in São Paulo or remote, and fluent in Portuguese and English.
What helps you stand out
LatAm corridor knowledge. Experience with Brazilian and wider LatAm payment rails, regulatory environments or banking partner ecosystems. Spanish is a plus alongside Portuguese.
Licensing and regulatory delivery. You have helped operationalise a licence, registration or scheme membership, not just tracked one.
Card network or payment scheme background. Time at a card network, payment scheme or large-scale processor with multi-market product launches.
Stablecoin or digital asset rails. Familiarity with stablecoin settlement, on and off-ramp infrastructure, or crypto payment products.

Equity in a rapidly growing company
The chance to work in a fast-paced startup at the forefront of fintech innovation
Real impact on global financial infrastructure
A collaborative culture with genuine emphasis on personal and professional growth

Product Manager (Interviews & Interview Assessment)
CAS Shield & Apply
📍 Location: Remote (with purpose-driven in-person meetups in London)
📝 Contract: Full-time, permanent
📅 Start Date: Immediate
💼 Reporting to: Deputy Director of CAS Shield, with a dotted line to the Deputy Director of Apply
🛂 Note: Candidates must be UK-based, have the right to work in the UK, and be able to travel to London for team meet-ups
About Enroly
At Enroly, we’re transforming the way universities recruit, assess and onboard international students. Our platforms are used by a significant share of UK higher education institutions to streamline compliance, reduce administrative burden, and improve the international student experience.

s.h: This role sits across our two core products
s.t:
CAS Shield — our flagship compliance and pre-CAS platform, trusted by nearly half of UK higher education institutions to manage visa readiness, credibility and onboarding at scale.
Apply — our application and admissions product, where institutions, agents and applicants come together at the very start of the student journey.
Enroly was recently acquired by Ecctis, the UK’s leading authority on international qualifications and skills benchmarking. Ecctis delivers essential services including qualification evaluation, recognition frameworks, and global consulting to governments, education providers, and employers. Together, we’re building a future-proofed approach to student recruitment and enrolment, backed by unparalleled data, insight, and capability.

We’re looking for a Product Manager to own Interviews and Interview Assessment across CAS Shield and Apply.
This is not a backlog-management role. You will be expected to define the product direction, make strategic trade-offs and establish how interviewing and assessment should work across Enroly's products.
Interviewing is one of the highest-stakes moments in the international student journey. Institutions use it to establish credibility, assess English language ability, and make admissions and compliance decisions that carry real regulatory weight. Applicants experience it on a mobile phone, often on a poor connection, in a different time zone, and frequently as their first direct interaction with the university.
Your job is to make that experience work — fair, credible, defensible and genuinely usable at scale. You’ll own the roadmap for asynchronous and live interviewing, assessment and scoring, and the integrity and proctoring capabilities that sit around them. This is a build-and-scale role: parts of this space are new, and you’ll be shaping direction as much as delivering against it.
This role suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, can balance applicant experience against institutional and regulatory needs, and is excited to define a product area rather than inherit one.

Own and drive the product roadmap for Interviews and Interview Assessment across both CAS Shield and Apply, aligned with Enroly’s company strategy.
Define the interviewing model: asynchronous and live formats, question design and banks, scoring rubrics, reviewer workflows, and assessment outputs institutions can act on and defend.
Own integrity and proctoring: identity verification, fraud and impersonation signals, AI-assisted detection, and the balance between assurance and a humane applicant experience.
Lead the mobile-first applicant experience — video capture, low-bandwidth resilience, accessibility, and drop-off reduction across devices and geographies.
Make the case for AI where it genuinely helps — transcription, summarisation, scoring support, anomaly detection — while keeping humans accountable for decisions.
Ensure interviews and assessment work coherently across two products, with a consistent experience for applicants and clear ownership boundaries internally.
Work directly with university admissions and compliance teams, agents, applicants and internal stakeholders to understand how interviews are created, completed, reviewed and used in admissions and compliance decisions.
Lead product discovery —Conduct discovery across the full interview lifecycle, including interview creation, applicant completion, assessment, reviewer workflows and institutional decision-making.
Work day-to-day with a dedicated squad: writing and refining user stories, managing backlogs, setting acceptance criteria, and collaborating closely with developers and QA.
Prioritise and execute improvements, from bug triage and fixes to new feature delivery, based on business impact and user feedback.
Post-launch analysis: track usage, completion and assessment quality, gather feedback, and use data to continuously iterate.
Champion compliance and regulatory requirements (e.g. UKVI credibility expectations, data protection, auditability) in product decisions and design.
Be the internal advocate for interviewing at Enroly, aligning teams around shared goals and user outcomes.
What Success Looks Like
High applicant completion rates and a demonstrably better interview experience, particularly on mobile.
Institutions trust the assessment output enough to make decisions on it — and can defend those decisions.
Interview integrity is measurably strong, with fraud and impersonation risk reduced without punishing genuine applicants.
Meaningful reduction in manual reviewer effort per interview.
Interviewing works as one coherent capability across CAS Shield and Apply.
Efficient prioritisation and execution of improvements and fixes.
Alignment with wider business and regulatory goals.
Who You’ll Work With
Product team: PMs, Designers, Solutions, Integrations
Tech team: Developers, QA — including mobile and AI/ML capability
Wider Enroly teams: Customer Success Managers, Compliance, Services, Marketing
Clients: university admissions and compliance teams, agent partners, and applicants
Challenges You’ll Tackle
Building a high-stakes, high-scrutiny product area where getting it wrong has real consequences for applicants and institutions.
Balancing integrity and assurance against applicant experience and completion.
Delivering a reliable video and mobile experience across highly variable devices, networks and geographies.
Serving two products with different lifecycles, users and delivery rhythms.
Working in an environment with limited resources and many competing voices.
Balancing short-term fixes with strategic improvements.
Navigating complex stakeholder landscapes in the education sector.
A growing team, evolving processes, and a high bar for quality.

Essential
3–4 years of experience in B2B SaaS product management.
Hands-on product experience in at least one of: asynchronous or video interviewing, remote proctoring or online assessment, identity verification, or another integrity-critical product area.
Experience delivering mobile or mobile-web products, with a real understanding of the constraints — device fragmentation, media capture, bandwidth, permissions, accessibility.
Strong execution skills: product discovery, prioritisation, delivery.
Fluency with qualitative and quantitative data.
Confident in internal and external stakeholder management, with strong communication and presentation skills.

Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.
We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, we have scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.
Locations: Remote. Open to candidates in Canada, Mexico, the United States, Brazil, and Colombia.

--------
You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.
The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.
The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve.

Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined.

The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.
You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

----------------
Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.
Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.
Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.
Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.
Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.
Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.
Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.
What you will need
------------------
You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.
Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.
You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.
You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.
You understand the accountant channel and how CPAs influence product adoption. Bonus if you have built for or partnered with CPAs directly.
Typically 4 to 10 years of experience. Title is not the point.

Additional Information
We want to hear from you. We value passion, determination, and honesty. If you do not match every line of the spec but you can show us the work, apply anyway. Unusual paths and rare skills are how you stand out at Flex.

At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. We believe everyone deserves a fair shot at success and appreciate the experiences each person brings beyond the traditional job requirements.

If you’re a close but not exact match with the description, we hope you’ll still consider applying. Want to learn more about life at Klaviyo? Visit klaviyo.com/careers to see how we empower creators to own their own destiny.

The Profiles Platform team owns Klaviyo’s core customer data system, the foundation that powers every product experience across the platform. This team is responsible for storing, managing, and serving customer profile data as the source of truth for downstream products like segmentation, flows, reporting, and analytics.

Their work ensures that profile data is accurate, scalable, and usable across the entire product ecosystem. From improving data modeling and computed properties to enabling enterprise-scale ingestion and supporting global compliance needs, this team plays a critical role in making Klaviyo’s platform intelligent and reliable at scale.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the strategy and roadmap for Klaviyo’s Profiles Platform. In this role, you will define how customer profile data is structured, processed, and served across the platform.

You’ll work at the intersection of data infrastructure, computed data, and scalability, ensuring that profile data remains trustworthy and performant as Klaviyo grows into more complex enterprise and global use cases. This is a high-impact platform role where your work will directly influence nearly every product team and customer experience.

Please note that this is an onsite role that requires 5 days/week in our Boston office. Fully remote candidates will not be considered at this time.
How You’ll Make a Difference
Own the strategy and roadmap for Klaviyo’s core profile data system, including profile traits, transformations, and storage layers
Serve as the product owner for the source of truth for customer data across the platform
Partner closely with engineering to evolve profile data architecture and services at massive scale
Collaborate with the Identity, Data, and Consent teams to ensure accurate and unified customer records
Drive improvements in profile data quality, usability, and modeling for downstream consumers (segmentation, flows, analytics, AI)
Enable enterprise and global expansion by supporting data residency, compliance, and regional infrastructure requirements
Define and track key metrics around data quality, performance, and system efficiency
What You’ll Work On
Building a computed properties platform to support derived traits (e.g., LTV, recency/frequency, propensity scoring)
Improving profile data modeling and transformations to make data more usable across the platform
Scaling ingestion systems to support billions of profiles and high-throughput workloads
Reducing cost and improving performance through sharding, traffic smoothing, and optimized write patterns
Supporting identity quality initiatives (e.g., deduplication, multi-email profiles, probabilistic matching)
Enabling regulated and global use cases, including data residency (e.g., EU, Japan) and compliance requirements

You have 6+ years of product management experience, ideally in platform, data infrastructure, or backend systems
You have experience working on data models, pipelines, or large-scale distributed systems
You are comfortable operating in highly technical environments and partnering closely with engineering
You have experience driving cross-team alignment across multiple stakeholders
You think in terms of systems and tradeoffs (scale, cost, performance, usability)
You can balance long-term platform investments with short-term product needs
You communicate clearly and can translate complex technical concepts into business impact

Experience with customer data platforms (CDPs) or identity systems
