Do you know what product management is really about? If you do, then you know it isn't roadmaps, tickets or beautifully groomed backlogs. It's finding a real, expensive, unglamorous problem that people live with every day - and shipping something that makes it go away. That is product.
At Shape Construction, we are building software that transforms how construction projects are delivered. It's born out of real project experience and designed to bring clarity, structure and performance to complex environments.
The problem we are solving is one of the oldest in the industry: what actually happens on a construction site never makes it, intact, to the people who need it. Supervisors, field engineers and site managers see reality first: work blocked, plans deviated from, instructions given verbally, conditions nobody planned for.

That knowledge lives in heads, notebooks, camera rolls and group chats. Meanwhile the people responsible for the commercial health of the project are working weeks behind, from whatever fragments they can piece together. By the time anyone needs to prove what happened, the evidence has gone cold.
We are building the platform that closes that gap. Tools the site genuinely wants to use, capturing what happens as it happens, and then turning that raw signal into structured, trustworthy records that let commercial and project leadership make decisions, hold their ground and protect margin they would otherwise have written off.
This is your opportunity to own a core part of that. You won't be handed a roadmap to administer, you'll shape it, defend it, and be measured on whether customers are genuinely better off. If you like being close to messy real-world problems, have strong opinions about what to build and the discipline to kill your own ideas when the evidence says so, keep reading.
(this will be a long write up but we like to give you all the details before you spend your time applying)
_________________________________________________________________________________________
We are Shape.Construction!
We are digitising the largest and most fundamental industry in the world, the industry that literally builds the foundations of the civilisation we all depend on to spare us from a brutal hunter-gatherer life: CONSTRUCTION
It is one of the least digitised industries in the world but also the largest - 1 in 9 people globally work in the construction industry and it constitutes 11% of global GDP.
Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. ( Watch our short film about it).
We got our start as a high-end construction project management consultancy. As a consultancy, we are focused on genuinely upgrading the way construction projects are delivered. We then take the deep understanding of the projects we work on to develop construction management software products that anyone can use to deliver their projects better.
We are building a full suite of products one module at a time - kind of like office 365 but for construction management - Check out Shape, our construction management tech
The core of all this is our true secret sauce; people. We only recruit the very best both in capability and personality. We are deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that is optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People that join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined.
This approach has allowed us to grow from just 2 people in 2017 to over 220 today (including consultancy) and we are still very much at the beginning! Joining us isn't just some "job", it is a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life.
4 core values for a good life
We believe a life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships with others and challenging yourself to create a positive impact. So our values reflect the 4 levels of relationships that each of us has:
Grow yourself - Your relationship with yourself
Care about people - Your relationship with others around you
Execute to greatness - Your relationship with your team
Build civilisation - Your relationship with humanity and the world
This goes much deeper but for the sake of brevity, we will keep the summary version!

s.t:

Connects us with meaningful relationships

As a Product Manager you'll own a core area of the Shape platform end to end, from the customer problem through to the outcome it produces on a live project.
You'll be accountable for a measurable business outcome for our customers, not for a feature list. Our platform spans two very different worlds, and both matter. On one side, the site: supervisors, field engineers and site managers working in conditions where an app has about five seconds to prove it's worth opening.

On the other, the office: project directors, commercial directors and quantity surveyors who need to trust what they're looking at enough to make a call on it. Value only appears when those two sides connect, and that connection is what we build.
Depending on where you're strongest and what the business needs, you might own the field side, the commercial side, or the seam between them. In every case the standard is the same: real adoption by people who have no obligation to use us, and a concrete outcome for the project as a result.
You'll also be at the front of how AI shows up in our products. A meaningful part of our ambition depends on AI doing genuinely hard things well in a domain with very little tolerance for confident nonsense, the stakes for our users are commercial and often contractual. You'll be the person who decides where AI earns its place, and where it doesn't.
Team
You'll be part of our Product team, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering, design, and our consultancy delivery teams, who are on live projects every day and are the sharpest feedback loop any product team could ask for. You'll also work closely with growth and customer success to make sure what we build reaches the people who need it.

Own the outcome: You will own a product area end to end, the problem, the strategy, the roadmap and the results. You'll define what success looks like in customer and commercial terms, and you'll be honest about whether we hit it.
Get close to the problem, on both sides: You'll spend real time on live projects, in the site cabin and in the commercial meeting, with our consultancy teams, and in the data. You'll build a deeper understanding of how a construction project actually runs, and of the commercial machinery behind it, than most people in our industry have, and use it to make sharp calls about what to build and what to refuse.

SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry.
By catering to both fans and rightsholders, we're powering a new, open entertainment ecosystem where fans have effortless access to experiences, and teams, venues, and shows have seamless access to their audiences. Because everyone should expect more from ticketing.
We are looking for Product Managers with varying levels of experience to join SeatGeek’s R&D team. This role will own SeatGeek's Catalog — the foundational data layer that defines what exists on our platform.

Impact of a Product Manager
As a Product Manager at Upsun, you own a significant area of Upsun Cloud, our cloud application platform, and the outcomes it delivers for the developers who build on it. The team you join owns the platform's foundations: the API, the runtime, environments, and the reliability every application running on Upsun depends on. And because Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love, much of what you build will be used by AI agents as much as by people.
This is a hands-on, technically rich role that bridges product strategy and deep infrastructure understanding. You own the strategy and the roadmap for your area, working closely with engineering to define platform behavior, build scalable abstractions, and shape workflows that empower modern development teams. Throughout, you act as the key voice for the user, making sure everything we ship contributes meaningfully to an exceptional developer experience.

Strategy and roadmap: Own the strategy, roadmap, and priorities for your area of Upsun Cloud, balancing established foundations with uncharted territory.

Software development background: Familiarity with building software using languages such as Python, Ruby, JavaScript, PHP, Go, or Rust.

About Chili Piper
Chili Piper is a B2B SaaS company that helps GTM teams turn inbound leads into qualified meetings - instantly. Our Demand Conversion Platform makes it easier for buyers and sellers to connect fast, without the usual friction in the funnel.
We’re a fully remote, global team that loves building solutions that truly help our customers, moving fast, and having fun while creating something meaningful. We’re growing quickly and aiming big!
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead Orchestrator, Chili Piper's GTM Control Layer.
Internally, we think of this role as a Product Market Fitter. This is not a traditional roadmap management role. It is a product leadership role for someone who loves building complex, enterprise-grade products and has the judgment to turn customer and market evidence into focused product bets that drive real adoption and business impact.
Orchestrator listens for signals across Chili Piper and external tools, decides what should happen next, and takes the action itself. That includes catching a form abandonment, a no-show, a missed meeting, or a cold chat, checking ICP fit, account ownership, intent history, and CRM state, then firing the right next step: enrolling a sequence in Salesloft, Outreach, or Gong Engage, notifying a rep, rescheduling a meeting, or sending a booking link.
You will own the full arc of a product bet: target customer, first audience, market and customer evidence, problem definition, intended outcome, value, viability, priority, success metrics, first adoption trigger, usage learning, and business outcome.
You will own the solution concept, meaning what we offer and how it is offered. You will not own solution architecture, implementation, or product enablement execution. You will partner closely with a Product Designer and a Product Engineering Lead to shape solutions that are valuable, coherent, and practical to deliver.
This role requires strong judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to turn complex workflows, data, and customer needs into clear product direction. It is a strong fit for someone who wants to build products that solve real problems for sophisticated users and who measures success by whether customers actually adopt what gets built.

s.h: Your Mission This is a company built for growth.
s.t:
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone. You'll work on real systems at a big scale, building high-performing consumer products used by millions. We move fast, cut the noise, and focus on what actually matters, because in our industry, speed wins.
We're rapidly scaling one of the most exciting innovations in mobile gaming: a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences. Our products are data-driven by design, powered by event-driven architectures, complex business logic, and quick feedback loops, with decisions informed by data and experimentation, not gut feeling.
As Senior Technical Product Manager (f/m/x) , this role isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform.

Product at exmox means understanding the bigger technical and business picture, working closely with Engineering, including how we use AI to move faster and cut down on repetitive work, and turning strategy into precise, technically grounded product decisions that create real value.

Every change you ship affects millions of users, and that responsibility is what makes working at exmox exciting.
If you're energized by fast-moving markets, complex technical systems, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.

Technical product strategy & vision Together with Engineering leads, you shape the product vision, strategy, and roadmap with a clear understanding of technical constraints and opportunities. You define goals and success metrics, and continuously evolve product direction based on system capabilities, technical debt, and business priorities.
Discovery, scoping & prioritization You gather and balance inputs from engineering, user research, data, and stakeholders to deeply understand problems, including their technical complexity. You write detailed, unambiguous requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineers can act on immediately.
Agile ownership & delivery You own the product backlog end-to-end: grooming, refinement, sprint planning, and prioritization. You actively participate in technical discussions, architecture reviews, and sprint ceremonies, ensuring the team always has well-defined, ready-to-build work.
Technical stakeholder alignment You translate business needs into precise engineering requirements, and translate technical realities back into language stakeholders understand. You work closely with Engineering, UI/UX, Data, Marketing, and Operations to ensure alignment across the full product lifecycle.
Experimentation & continuous improvement You leverage A/B testing, analytics, and system monitoring to validate ideas, measure outcomes, and drive ongoing product and technical improvements. You understand data pipelines and instrumentation well enough to define the right metrics from the ground up.
What You Bring Technical Product Manager experience Strong experience as a Technical Product Manager building digital products, ideally in mobile gaming, ad-tech, e-commerce, or online marketing. You've worked closely with engineering teams and are comfortable in technical conversations.
Engineering fluency You don't need to code, but you can read and discuss API contracts, system architectures, database schemas, and technical trade-offs. Engineers see you as a peer, not just a requirements writer.
Agile ownership You have deep hands-on experience owning a product backlog: writing epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria, running sprint ceremonies, and continuously improving team throughput and focus.
Data-driven product decisions Solid experience using quantitative data, A/B testing, funnel analysis, and product analytics tools to guide decisions. You understand how data is collected, structured, and interpreted, and can define instrumentation requirements yourself.
High-scale product teams At least 4 years of experience working with cross-functional engineering and product teams on high-scale digital products with millions of users.
Discovery & problem solving Strong analytical and structured thinking skills. You can break down complex technical and product problems, identify root causes, and drive toward clear, testable solutions.
Ownership mindset You unblock teams, remove ambiguity, and take accountability for outcomes, not just outputs. You're persistent, solution-oriented, and comfortable making calls with incomplete information.
Clear communicator across technical and non-technical audiences Outstanding at adapting communication style: precise and detailed with engineers, strategic and impact-focused with leadership and business stakeholders.
Structured & organized Able to manage multiple workstreams, balance competing priorities, and deliver against realistic timelines without losing sight of the bigger picture
How We Win Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.
Please note: this is not a remote only position, we offer you a flexible hybrid model here in Hamburg, Germany - working from home on Mondays & Fridays, coming to the office on Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday!

We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.
When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

Exzellente schriftliche Kommunikation (Roadmaps, PRDs).
AI-Erfahrung am Puls der Zeit: Du bist bei neuen Entwicklungen up-to-date und findest wege, wie du AI für Deine Arbeit und eingebettet im Softwareteam effizient nutzen kannst.
Fließend Deutsch, sehr gutes Englisch.
Das wäre ein Plus
Erfahrung mit Prozessen aus der Warenwirtschaft oder aus dem Handel.
Ein Software-Background kombiniert mit Product-Management-Erfahrung.
Aufgabenbereich
Was du bei uns bewegst
Du verantwortest die Produktstrategie und -roadmap für den Bereich Grower Experience.
Du sprichst wöchentlich eigenständig mit unseren Gärtner*innen, baust Beziehungen zu ihnen auf und triffst die Betriebe in unregelmäßigen Abständen auch vor Ort.
Du arbeitest eng mit Design und Engineering zusammen, leitest gemeinsam mit Design User Interviews und übersetzt die daraus gewonnenen Erkenntnisse in konkrete Produktentscheidungen, während Du das Team fachlich durch den gesamten Produktentwicklungsprozess führst.
Du verstehst und artikulierst den Business Value deiner Produktentscheidungen, u. a. über KPI-Frameworks, und nutzt Tracking- und Analytics-Daten, um Annahmen zu validieren und Produktentscheidungen datenbasiert zu treffen.
Du kommunizierst Roadmaps, PRDs und Produktentscheidungen klar und überzeugend – schriftlich wie mündlich.
Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich in deinem Alltag – für Prototyping, eigene Datenanalysen und einen effizienten, AI-gestützten Produktentwicklungsprozess gemeinsam mit deinem Engineering-Team.
Deine Arbeit hat direkten Einfluss auf unser Produkt, unsere Kunden und den Erfolg von June.
So arbeiten wir
Unsere Produktteams verantworten ihre Bereiche vollständig: von der Produktstrategie über User Research und Priorisierung bis hin zum Release und den kommerziellen KPIs ihres Bereichs.
Gemeinsam mit Design und Engineering übernehmt ihr Verantwortung für den Erfolg eures Produktbereichs und arbeitet kontinuierlich daran, ihn zu verbessern.
Wir sprechen regelmäßig mit unseren Kunden, besuchen sie vor Ort und testen unsere Lösungen gemeinsam mit ihnen. Wir glauben, dass gute Produktentscheidungen nur entstehen, wenn man die Probleme der Nutzer wirklich versteht.
Wir arbeiten pragmatisch, treffen Entscheidungen früh und passen sie an, wenn neue Erkenntnisse entstehen. Wir haben starke Meinungen, halten aber nicht dogmatisch an ihnen fest. Verantwortung endet bei uns nicht mit dem Release.

About Lucidya
Lucidya is an AI-native platform for customer experience (CX) intelligence that helps organizations understand, engage, and retain customers at scale.
Unlike traditional platforms that stop at reporting and dashboards, Lucidya combines proprietary AI, deep language understanding, and autonomous workflows to help organizations move from insight to action. Our technology is built in-house and trained on millions of multilingual customer conversations, enabling brands across the MENA region to make better decisions, deliver better experiences, and build stronger customer relationships.
As AI reshapes how businesses operate, we're building products that make customer understanding faster, more accurate, and more actionable than ever before.
Why This Role Matters
Most organizations today are overwhelmed with customer data.
Conversations are happening across social media, surveys, reviews, support tickets, messaging channels, and countless other touchpoints. The challenge isn't collecting the data anymore. It's knowing what matters and what to do next.
The Monitoring & Research domain sits at the center of that challenge.
This is where customers come to understand public perception, identify emerging trends, monitor competitors, measure customer sentiment, and uncover the insights that drive business decisions. It is one of the most strategically important parts of Lucidya 's platform and one of the biggest opportunities for innovation as AI transforms how research and customer intelligence are done.
As Senior Product Manager, you'll be responsible for shaping how thousands of users discover, trust, and act on insights generated from millions of customer conversations.
You'll be joining a team that values ownership over hierarchy, customer outcomes over feature output, and learning over certainty. We move quickly, challenge assumptions, and expect product leaders to bring strong opinions while remaining open to changing their minds when the evidence says otherwise.
If you're excited by complex customer problems, AI-powered products, and the opportunity to define the future of customer intelligence in a region where world-class solutions are still emerging, this role will give you significant room to make an impact.

Own the future of Monitoring & Research at Lucidya
You'll define the vision, strategy, and roadmap across three key product areas:
Social Listening
Managed Channels Analytics
Voice of Customer (VoC)
Your responsibility isn't simply delivering features. It's ensuring customers can confidently answer critical business questions about their customers, markets, competitors, and brand performance.
Turn customer signals into decisions
You'll spend significant time understanding how customers currently make decisions, where they struggle to find trustworthy insights, and what prevents them from taking action.
You'll use those learnings to build products that help customers move beyond reporting and toward clear recommendations, meaningful insights, and measurable business outcomes.
Lead discovery before delivery
You'll challenge assumptions, validate problems, and ensure we're solving issues that matter before resources are committed.
You'll regularly engage customers, prospects, Customer Success teams, and internal stakeholders to uncover opportunities and validate product direction.
Success in this role means building the right thing, not simply building things quickly.
Raise the quality bar for AI-powered insights
As AI becomes increasingly central to our platform, you'll help define what "trustworthy AI" means in practice.
You'll work closely with AI, Data, Design, and Engineering teams to improve:
Insight accuracy
Sentiment quality
Explainability
Relevance
Customer trust
You'll constantly ask whether an insight is genuinely useful, not just technically impressive.
Make difficult prioritization decisions
Not every good idea belongs on the roadmap.
You'll evaluate opportunities using customer feedback, product data, market insights, commercial priorities, and strategic impact.
You'll make trade-offs transparently and help the organization understand why certain bets are worth making while others are not.
Drive product adoption and business impact
You'll closely monitor customer behavior, adoption patterns, retention drivers, churn signals, and feedback loops.
You'll use those insights to continuously improve the product and ensure the work being delivered creates measurable value for both customers and the business.
Be a leader beyond product
You'll collaborate across Engineering, Design, AI, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and Leadership teams.
You'll help create alignment, provide clarity during ambiguity, and contribute to building a culture where teams are empowered to solve problems rather than simply execute requirements.

You have strong product fundamentals
You have at least 5 years of product management experience, ideally within B2B SaaS environments.
You know how to take a problem from discovery through validation, delivery, measurement, and iteration.
You understand that product management is ultimately about creating customer and business value, not managing backlogs.
You simplify complexity
You're comfortable working with large datasets, analytics platforms, AI-powered products, or technically complex systems.
More importantly, you know how to transform complexity into experiences that feel intuitive and useful to customers.
You stay close to customers
You don't rely solely on internal opinions to make decisions.
You regularly speak with customers, investigate workflows, validate assumptions, and seek evidence before committing to a direction.
You're naturally curious about how people work and where products create friction in their lives.
You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information
You won't always have perfect data.
You can balance analysis with action, make informed decisions under uncertainty, and adapt when new information becomes available.
You communicate with clarity
You can explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and customer problems to technical teams.
You build alignment through clear thinking, structured communication, and transparency.
You care about outcomes
You measure success by customer adoption, customer value, and business impact rather than the number of features released.
You're willing to challenge existing thinking when you believe there's a better way to solve a problem.

Experience with social listening, media monitoring, Voice of Customer, customer intelligence, or research platforms
Experience building AI-powered, analytics-heavy, or data-intensive products
Familiarity with sentiment analysis, NLP, LLMs, recommendation systems, or automated research workflows
Experience working with Arabic-language products, dialects, or regional customer behaviors
Knowledge of MENA markets, particularly Saudi Arabia and the GCC
Experience with platforms such as Brandwatch, Sprinklr, Meltwater, Talkwalker, Qualtrics, Medallia, or Brand24
What Success Looks Like

Technical Product Manager Level 3
Importance: High

The Technical Product Manager (TPM) primarily owns and drives platform products through vision, design, requirements, and delivery. This includes driving the strategy for platform domains, setting objectives and key results (OKRs), and ensuring their successful completion.

The TPM will facilitate a larger cross-functional team to solve business problems. The TPM should be able to work with significant autonomy and freedom, requiring little oversight, but within a broader strategy set by executive leadership.

The TPM will demonstrate the companys core values of respect, honesty, integrity, diversity, inclusion, and safety.
There are 5 technology Tracks defined for KAP. Each TPM is responsible for a Track. The Tracks are:
1. Development All tools and processes developers use to develop, test, and deploy applications.
2. Platform Tools and processes where applications run (e.g., cloud, on-prem).
3. Operations & Support Tools and processes used to ensure an application is running effectively (e.g., logging, tracing, monitoring, alerting).
4. Data Management Tools and process used in data storage and movement (e.g., DBMS, caching, queues).
5. Native Mobile Tools and processes needed to develop, deploy, and support applications written for Android or iOS.
This position will focus on the Development Track.

Exceptional communication, organization, and analytical skills Experience leading and managing a team with direct and indirect reports
Demonstrated experience creating and using strategy to solve complex problems that span across multiple divisions and groups within company
Ability to identify metrics and key performance measures and use data to drive decisions which enhance the customer experience

3+ years product management experience at a retailer or digital platform company

Experience using GitHub, Atlassian, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud products
Since this TPM will be working directly with development teams, a background in software development is advantageous.

Define KAP product strategy, features and criteria for evaluating vendors/partners to make ongoing buy-build-partner-acquire decisions
Create highly collaborative cross-functional partnerships across, Kroger Technology & Digital, 84.51, Alt Profits, Merchandising, Manufacturing, Retail Operations, Supply Chain, Health & Wellness, Marketing, and Finance
Identify opportunities to create best-in-class platform capabilities by leveraging customer/developer feedback, monitoring/analytics, and team know-how/ know-why in order to connect company strengths with available resources

NovaKid is a global leader in online English education for children aged 4–12, serving 100000+ students across 50+ countries. As the Product Manager for AI & Game-Based Learning, you will own the "non-live" student experience.
Your goal is to transform the Novakid Kid’s Area from a supplementary area into a significant driver of language acquisition for young kids. You will lead the development of self-guided English learning games and integrate cutting-edge AI-based self-practice tools that encourage children to speak more, practice safely, and stay motivated between their 1:1 teacher sessions.
Focus: Kid’s Area, Self-Learning Games, and AI Features

Lead a small team of designers and developers (with access to analytical and research resources).
Design and scale features like Pandy AI Tutor to provide 24/7, judgment-free speaking practice for students across various proficiencies.
Own the roadmap for current and future gamified worlds, focusing on LLM based learning mini-games that reinforce curriculum-aligned vocabulary and grammar.
Use AI to create adaptive learning paths that adjust game difficulty and content in real-time based on a child’s performance in both live classes and self-study.
Work with engineering to refine Speech-to-Text and AI prompting logic to maximize student speaking time—aiming for the high-engagement levels seen in AI-only learning models.
Design and manage the "Economy of Fun," including avatars, star rewards, and other gamification features that compete for a child's attention against mainstream apps.
Work closely with designers, engineers, curriculum developers, and teacher operations to turn user insights into high-quality educational content and engaging UX.

4+ years’ experience in a PM role.
Hands-on experience in AI-powered features (prompt engineering, conversational AI, or adaptive algorithms).
Strong background in mobile gaming or highly gamified EdTech, with a deep understanding of reward systems, level progression, and retention hooks.
Proven ability to build interfaces for 4–12-year-olds that are intuitive, safe, and require zero parental intervention.
Proficiency in analytical tools to analyze "incidental learning" metrics and game-completion rates.
Manage the Agile process with our engineering team, ensuring that prototypes are delivered and scaled with technical excellence.
You thrive in a 100% remote, distributed team environment and are a master of tools like JIRA and Slack.
Excellent spoken and written English.
Fully remote work (core hours GMT+3).

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies.

Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request.

As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools.

Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up.

If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
Available Locations: Austin, TX | London, UK | Lisbon, Portugal
About the Department
The Product Management team at Cloudflare steers the strategy, roadmap, and execution that powers a faster, more secure internet. As part of the Zero Trust Security organization, our mission is to redefine corporate networking and security. We build solutions that protect users, devices, and data globally without sacrificing performance, replacing legacy architectures with our modern, identity-aware global network.

You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap, and execution for the Cloudflare One Browser Extension. You will also work alongside the Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) and WARP Client teams, heavily influencing their direction and owning selected initiatives as customer needs and business priorities evolve.
This role combines focused ownership with range. You will take an emerging product from early adoption to a scaled enterprise capability, while moving across adjacent Cloudflare One priorities where strong product leadership is needed. More than narrow domain expertise, success requires exceptional problem solving, sound judgment, and the ability to quickly understand and lead in new technical areas. This work will help advance Cloudflare’s long-term position in SASE and SSE.
This is a high-judgment role. Success requires navigating conflicting customer signals, making trade-offs with incomplete information, and building trust across engineering and sales teams—work that demands human context and accountability and cannot be delegated to automation.

Own Browser Extension: Set the strategy, roadmap, and execution plan for Cloudflare One Browser Extension. Grow it into a trusted enterprise product that addresses meaningful browser security and visibility needs, integrates naturally with Cloudflare One, and earns sustained customer adoption.
Shape the Enterprise Client and Digital Experience: Work alongside the WARP Client and DEX teams to improve how customers deploy, operate, and troubleshoot Cloudflare One. Influence product direction, connect customer needs across the browser, device, and network, and own selected initiatives when dedicated leadership will accelerate an important outcome.
Drive Product Strategy: Connect browser, device, and network capabilities into a coherent Cloudflare One experience. Set clear priorities across products at different stages of maturity and adjust ownership as new opportunities emerge.
Talk to Customers: Work directly with enterprise security, networking, and IT teams to understand their most important problems. Translate those needs into focused product decisions without overfitting to individual customer requests.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate closely with Engineering, Product Marketing, Sales, Support, and adjacent product teams to deliver high-impact products from concept to global launch.
Data-Informed Decision Making: Analyze product usage, reliability, support signals, market trends, and competitive capabilities to identify opportunities, make trade-offs, and measure customer outcomes.

Demonstrated Product Leadership: Experience managing technically complex B2B products through the full product lifecycle, with a record of finding the right problem, setting a clear direction, and shipping products customers value.
AI Fluency: Demonstrated experience using AI assistants, coding tools, and agentic workflows to accelerate product work. You should be comfortable in an AI-native environment where tools like OpenCode are standard infrastructure, not optional perks.
Strategic Problem Solving: Proven track record of quickly understanding unfamiliar problem spaces, turning ambiguous technical challenges into clear plans, and prioritizing the work that will have the greatest impact.
Exceptional Communication: Strong ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly to both engineering teams and non-technical business stakeholders.
Judgment Under Ambiguity: Proven ability to synthesize incomplete or conflicting signals, make difficult trade-offs, and take accountability for outcomes.

Working knowledge of modern browsers and enterprise client software, including deployment, configuration, update lifecycles, telemetry, security controls, and operating-system constraints.
Ability to reason across endpoint, DNS, HTTP, TLS, proxy, VPN, Wi-Fi, ISP, and application layers and turn difficult diagnostic problems into clear product experiences.
Experience with Chromium-based browsers, browser extension APIs, managed browser deployment, or device management platforms.
Experience with Digital Experience Monitoring, endpoint observability, synthetic testing, or network diagnostics.
Understanding of Zero Trust and SASE products such as secure web gateways, data loss prevention, remote browser isolation, Zero Trust Network Access, and enterprise VPN clients.
Experience designing privacy-sensitive telemetry and administrative controls for enterprise products.

About Customer Portal
Customer Portal exists to make Veriff's product sell itself. The Portal serves two purposes. It allows our customers to operate Veriff products — setting up and configuring products, consulting verification session details, reporting issues.

And it is a privileged surface for customers to discover, try, buy and expand through a seamless self-serve experience, connecting product usage, onboarding and growth in one place. It unites forces with GTM to automate acquisition, upsell, cross-sell and retention, with end-to-end ownership of the customer persona. The area is evolving fast.

What began as a self-serve growth surface (Station) is becoming the customer-facing window into Veriff's accuracy and fraud advantage for our largest enterprise customers.
The shape of this role
This is an IC-first leadership role, and the first genuine step into product leadership — distinct from a strong senior IC. At first you will lead through craft, authority and influence. You own the strategy, discovery, roadmap and delivery for your product area.
As you refine the strategic themes for this large product, we expect you to propose the team configuration needed to support our growth and company objectives. That will move you progressively from IC to manager, while retaining hands-on ownership of at least one part of the Customer Portal area in the mid-term. We will deliberately assess for both the IC craft bar and the latent management capability, because the role is designed to traverse the line.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the Customer Portal area, tied explicitly to Veriff's commercial model and revenue drivers.
Run disciplined, continuous discovery with customers, and translate it into well-defined problem statements and a sequenced roadmap.
Make transparent prioritisation and trade-off calls across product ambition, technical sustainability and business urgency — especially where capability gaps mean we cannot do everything at once.
Define success metrics before building, and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not output.
Partner as a credible peer to Engineering, GTM, Fraud Ops and Design. Be the connective tissue that turns internal expertise into a customer-facing product.
Own launch as a discipline from the start — internal platform releases and external GTM — not a milestone at the end.
Set and uphold the product-craft bar. Mentor PMs and, in time, build and lead the team.
Champion AI internally, implementing new best practices for faster product discovery and delivery.

You are a product leader who has earned authority through the quality of your thinking rather than a title.
You have owned a product area end-to-end
From strategy through discovery, delivery and launch. You are equally comfortable in the messy front end of a problem and in the discipline of shipping.
You are looking for the step where your impact starts to come through others, and you are excited that this role begins as an individual leader and grows into managing a team — not the other way around.
You think commercially
You instinctively connect what you build to how the business grows, and you explain the “why” behind a product bet in terms of revenue, retention and customer trust, not just features and flows.
You run discovery as a continuous discipline
You get close to customers, including demanding enterprise accounts, and you can tell the difference between what they ask for and what they actually need.
You turn that into sharp problem statements and a phased roadmap where every step delivers a real customer outcome.
You prioritise ruthlessly and transparently
When there are more good ideas than capacity, you make the hard calls about what not to do, and you can articulate the reasoning.
You define success before you build. When something goes wrong, you own it without deflection and change how you work as a result.
You lead through influence, not authority
You build credibility with engineering, go-to-market, design and operations partners as a genuine peer, and you reach good decisions with people who do not report to you.
You stay calm under uncertainty, create space for views that differ from your own, and commit gracefully once a call is made.
You raise the people around you
You set a high craft bar through your own work, share your thinking generously and give specific, useful feedback.
You are motivated by building and leading a team over time, with a realistic understanding that management is a different job — one focused on developing people and multiplying impact, not doing all the work yourself.
You stay current on your craft
You take pride in tracking how product management is evolving, and you consistently find time to experiment and fold what works into your practice.

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.
We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.
When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.
The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.
The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.
In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.
This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week.

Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Set the quality bar and release criteria for search: what good means per use case, and what a change has to clear before it ships. Our evaluation team owns the measurement, and you work closely with them on what to measure and why.
Own the depth, latency, and cost tradeoffs across our search products, and make them explicit and defensible.
Shape the direction of our index: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what quality bar it has to meet.
Build a point of view on where search infrastructure is going as agents, rather than people, become the main consumer, and turn that into a roadmap.
Know how we compare to the alternatives customers evaluate, and drive the work that closes the gaps that matter.
Work with customer success and directly with customers to understand where our results fall short in real workflows, and turn that into quality priorities.
Partner with the data and vertical product owners on what our corpus needs to contain and how results should be shaped per industry.

5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion spent on high-scale search or ranking systems: web search, feed ranking at a large social platform, or a large ad engine.
A background as an engineer, ML engineer, or researcher on a production system in one of those areas. This is a requirement rather than a preference. You will be making tradeoff calls alongside senior search engineers, and you need to have built something at that scale yourself.
Direct experience shipping a search or ranking change end to end, including how it was evaluated and what happened after it shipped.
A strong data foundation: you can design an experiment, read eval results critically, and tell a real quality improvement from noise.
Product judgment to match the technical depth: you can decide what to build and what to leave, and defend it to both engineers and customers.
Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how retrieval fits into agentic workflows.
Comfort with ambiguity, moving between strategy and execution without losing the thread.
The ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a systems-minded Staff Product Manager to take Constructor’s search and discovery to the state of the art — and keep it there — across every retail industry we serve. This is a highly technical, high-leverage role at the core of our Product Discovery Engine chapter: the teams responsible for how we retrieve, understand, and rank the right products for every shopper, on every query, for every customer.
Your job is to raise discovery quality and, through it, our customers’ business metrics. You won’t be measured on features shipped — you’ll be measured on relevance and business outcomes, like conversion, revenue per visit, and search-attributed GMV, moving up.
You’ll start embedded with our Search Quality team, owning its strategy and roadmap and getting deep into the systems that decide what shoppers actually see. Over time, your mandate grows to setting direction for the entire Product Discovery Engine chapter — deciding where we’re heading and why across recall, ranking, query understanding, personalization, and the ML infrastructure underneath. This is a Staff role today with a clear path to Director as you take on chapter-wide leadership.
Search at Constructor is fundamentally a machine learning problem, so this role lives and breathes ML. You’ll partner closely with ML, data science, and engineering to turn the latest research into production wins, keep us ahead of both commercial competitors and academic state of the art, and be the connective tissue that aligns multiple teams — ML Recall, ML Infra, and, over time, teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management — behind a single, coherent vision for great discovery.
If you’re excited about driving innovation across dozens of the world’s largest retailers, being held to relevance and business outcomes, and pushing an already best-in-class product further ahead, this role is for you.

Own business impact, not features. Drive measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV alongside relevance across our customer base.
Deliver across every retail industry. Move quality and business metrics across all the verticals we serve, accounting for the differences in catalog, language, and shopper intent.
Keep us at the state of the art. Continuously translate the latest ML / IR research and competitive moves into production wins, and ship SOTA ML / LLM-assisted capabilities that beat our previous best on relevance.
Set chapter vision and strategy. Define the multi-quarter direction for the Product Discovery Engine — where we’re heading and why — tie it directly to customer business outcomes, and rally teams behind it.
Lead Search Quality first. Own its strategy and roadmap, driving measurable improvements in the relevance and correctness of results.
Orchestrate across the pipeline. Unify recall, ranking, query understanding, and personalization behind one definition of quality and one set of business metrics, so improvements compound instead of colliding.
Turn ML research into production wins. Partner deeply with ML and data science to take models — from candidate generation and recall to LLM-assisted interpretation — from idea to production, balancing accuracy, latency, and cost.
Make quality measurable and explainable. Build the metrics, evaluation frameworks, and tooling the whole chapter uses to measure, attribute, and explain discovery quality and its business impact.
Own quality under pressure. Lead investigation and triage when issues arise, and design durable, systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.
Grow the mandate. Expand into chapter-wide leadership spanning ML Recall, ML Infra, and — over time — teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management.
What Success Looks Like

About Hightouch
Hightouch is an Agentic Marketing Platform powered by the industry-leading Composable CDP. With complete brand context, customer data, and performance history in one place, every marketer finally has the power to build and ship end-to-end campaigns themselves. Teams move faster, stay on brand, and get AI marketing that actually works.
Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, Hightouch enables marketing teams to analyze performance, brainstorm ideas, and generate creative at a speed and quality that wasn't previously possible.
Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Customer Data Platforms, Hightouch is trusted by leading enterprises like Domino's, Spotify, Aritzia, Cars.com, Ramp, and PetSmart.
At Hightouch , our mission is to help our customers leverage data and AI to grow their businesses. The team is ambitious, impact-driven, efficient — and we believe humility, kindness, and compassion are essential to our success. If you're energized by velocity, obsessed with raising the bar, and want to build alongside people who care deeply about each other and our customers, we'd love to meet you.
About the Product Team
You’ll join a lean, world-class Product Team. We’ve thought deeply about what winning product culture looks like in competitive markets being reshaped by AI. The team prizes founder-level commercial instinct, the bandwidth to cover broad areas, and extremely fast iteration aided by product-minded engineers and AI. We’re the team that invented Reverse ETL, pioneered the Composable architecture, landed AI Decisioning as a category, and most recently invented Agentic Marketing.
Why this role matters
This portfolio is the majority of Hightouch 's revenue — and it deserves a single, dedicated owner. Audiences, traits, experiments, analytics, and orchestration are the surfaces our customers live in every day, but the unifying vision across them has so far been carried by founders and shared across the team. We're hiring this role to change that: one person accountable for the health, direction, and growth of our core.
What you’ll own
We're looking for a product leader for the core surface area of Hightouch : the interfaces marketers live in every day and the largest driver of our revenue. You'll own a broad portfolio spanning:
Audiences — the segmentation and targeting experience at the center of Hightouch
Charts & Dashboards — analytics surfaces for customers to uncover audience insights and monitor performance
Experiments — automation and measurement tools to run & monitor cross-channel experiments
Trait Building — no-code interfaces to build custom business logic and data attributes to power marketing campaigns
Orchestration — primitives for how campaigns and journeys are sequenced and coordinated globally across all of Hightouch
We need someone who can drive clarity, set prioritization, and bring a unifying vision across that entire portfolio.

The role’s mandate spans multiple modes of product work: from 0-1 innovation to deepening established surfaces to scaling emerging areas. A significant part of the job will be deciding what to prioritize and what outcomes to achieve in which order to hit our company revenue goals. Some examples include:
Building 0→1 in global orchestration: defining the right audience, campaign and journey primitives for AI-native, Fortune 100-class marketing programs
Expanding audience targeting & syncing to better support advanced use cases like couponing and live auctions
Transforming our investment in charts, dashboards, and experimentation to better interface with Hightouch Agentic Marketing
This is a senior, hands-on role — think “product GM.” You'll be fully accountable for both product adoption and go-to-market success, leading across multiple Engineering and Design workstreams. You'll present frequently to customers, work directly with executives, and shape company strategy.

Customer Obsession: You are a relentless customer champion. Your superpower is the ability to forge deep connections, intuitively anticipating needs before customers can even articulate them.
Technical Aptitude: More than just understanding technical concepts, you're a translator who turns complex engineering challenges into elegant, accessible solutions. You speak both engineer and business fluently.
Strong Communicator: You can drive clarity and distill complex ideas into compelling narratives that inspire teams and resonate with users, turning insights into action.
Hunger and Speed: Speed isn't just a preference for you—it's a way of life. You thrive in a high-energy environment where rapid iteration and bold moves are the default, not the exception.
Outcome Mindset: You're not a feature factory—you're a strategic mastermind who reverse-engineers success. Every decision you make is laser-focused on driving measurable business impact, turning product vision into tangible results.

Outschool’s mission is to inspire kids to love learning. In our fast-changing world, the traditional educational system struggles to meet the diverse and evolving needs of young learners. Outschool reimagines this system, offering flexible and engaging learning experiences as a supplement and alternative to traditional education. By connecting learners with a global community of teachers and peers through our online platform, we make learning personal, dynamic, and deeply human.
We've made significant strides since launching our marketplace of live online classes in 2017. Finding initial success with secular homeschoolers, we then expanded to enrichment learning to meet the needs of a wider audience, growing our business 16x since 2019.

Post-pandemic, we have evolved our platform to power academic learning, incorporated AI, and have begun to grow our international community. We're proud to have served over 1.5M passionate learners with more than $100M in annual bookings.
Driving disruptive, positive change in education is rewarding and hard. Outschool team members are encouraged to challenge themselves, take risks, and grow in their careers. Healthcare should work for patients, but it doesn’t. In their time of need, they call down outdated insurance directories. Then wait on hold. Then wait weeks for the privilege of a visit. Then wait in a room solely designed for waiting. Then wait for a surprise bill. In any other consumer industry, the companies delivering such a poor customer experience would not survive. But in healthcare, patients lack market power. Which means they are expected to accept the unacceptable.
Zocdoc’s mission is to give power to the patient. To do that, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace that makes it easy to find and book in-person or virtual care in all 50 states, across 200+ specialties and +12k insurance plans. By giving patients the ability to see and choose, we give them power.

In doing so, we can make healthcare work like every other consumer sector, where businesses compete for customers, not the other way around. In time, this will drive quality up and prices down.
We’re 18 years old and the leader in our space, but we are still just getting started. If you like solving important, complex problems alongside deeply thoughtful, driven, and collaborative teammates, read on.

Vous êtes autonome, pragmatique, structuré(e) et orienté(e) solutions. Vous savez faire avancer les sujets, prioriser, prendre des décisions et collaborer efficacement avec des interlocuteurs métier, techniques et externes.

Frame the problem, define the hypothesis, and choose the fastest route to signal: interviews, prototypes, fake doors, experiments, or just shipping and measuring

Decision oriented: You know when there's enough signal to move. You sharpen hypotheses, clarify thinking, and make confident calls under uncertainty. You'd rather ship and learn than perfect and wait.

Anyone can build AI insurance software now. The models are commoditized. The demos work. Almost nobody starts where Agency Revolution starts: thousands of independent P&C agencies already paying us to communicate with their clients, plus deep integrations into the systems where agency data actually lives.
The opportunity is the relationship layer — the system that notices when an agency's clients are at risk of churning, spots the cross-sell opportunity, picks the right message and channel and moment, and acts. We call it RelationshipOS. For ten years, agencies have trusted us to speak to their clients.

Now we're expanding what we can see: call transcripts, carrier communications, life events. The policies live in the agency's management system. The relationship lives with us. Nobody else has both the permission and the infrastructure.
We know what we're betting on. We don't yet know what makes an agency owner act on it. That's the job.
The strategic thesis is set. What's unresolved is whether it's true — whether an agency will actually change what they do because our system told them to, and what has to be built for that to happen. You're hired to answer that by shipping, not by studying.

s.h: Two halves, and you need both
s.t:
You personally build the bet. The intelligence layer is your work. Discovery with agency owners, prototypes in front of them within days, the smallest version that proves someone will act. Much of this is assembled rather than authored — the right vendor wired into AR Connect and pointed at a real use case will beat anything we could build from scratch this year. You don't hand this half to your team; it's too early and too ambiguous to delegate.
Your team drives the day-to-day execution and health of the existing platform. Two Product Owners and a Product Analyst keep a profitable, decade-old product healthy and improving. You set their priorities, strengthen their product judgment, raise their craft, and shield them from thrash. You remain the primary product manager responsible for the roadmap, discovery, and strategic product decisions. Done well, this is what buys you the time to do the first half.
Most people are good at one of these. We need someone who won't quietly abandon the other.
This position offers $125,000-$140,000 depending on experience and qualifications.

RelationshipOS — the intelligence layer. Churn signals. Cross-sell opportunities. Adaptive customer journeys instead of rigid sequences. You define what "acted on" means, instrument it, and are accountable for the number.
AR Connect and the vendor stack. AR Connect is our integration layer — where APIs pull in calls, carrier communications, life events, and other signals, and where third-party capability plugs into our distribution. It's the substrate the whole thesis sits on, and it's how a promising vendor becomes a live use case in front of agencies.
That work is yours: mapping the landscape of management systems, carrier connections, data enrichment providers, and AI vendors; deciding what we integrate versus build; running the POCs; and getting from "interesting demo" to something an agency actually uses. Data quality, latency, unit economics, and what happens when a vendor's model is wrong are your problems to surface early. You shape the deals and bring the recommendation — the SVP and our partnership team close them.
Voice AI as a channel. Not a feature — a real channel. Define the MVP, run pilots where AI handles outbound outreach with warm handoffs to agencies, and produce the evidence for whether this moves us from subscription toward outcome-based pricing.
The Agency Revolution roadmap. What ships, in what order, and what we stop doing. You own the sequencing and defend it.
